test(lanes): a session's drawn bar carries its session-pane ⚠, through the draw a request takes (candybar-gather-renderer-76bb.1dh.trm) (#675)

* test(lanes): a session's drawn bar carries its session-pane ⚠, through the draw a request takes (candybar-gather-renderer-76bb.1dh.trm)

The checkpoint stamps each tick from its Claude Code's record on the disk,
the request arm records the mismatch run in its turn, and the daemon's draw
lists the ⚠; the list is read from the session's recording. An unconfirmed
stamp and a lasted mismatch each list the session-pane message; a confirmed
tick, a mismatch inside the race and a /clear straggler list none.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(lanes): the pane-draw ticks take the daemon's reply, and a /clear's stragglers cross the race (candybar-gather-renderer-76bb.1dh.trm)

High review of #675:
- The straggler case could not fail: its ticks never crossed the race, so
  a broken rewrite-race exemption passed. Its stragglers now land at 1s,
  race-1s and race+2s after the new session's first tick.
- Each tick goes through replyTo, with the home as the daemon passes it
  and a deadline already due, instead of a hand copy of its render arm.
- The session store is held by the journal turns; teardown closes the
  host service, the turns and the store, as the daemon's does.
- A tick that logs an error fails.
- The messages are asserted by the facts that tell the stamps apart;
  their wording is the unit test's.

Breaking the exemption, the draw's run lookup, or its lasted check each
fails a case. The shared in-worker draw-parts helper is .5hr.

* test(lanes): each pane-draw case that draws no ⚠ shows the lane could draw one (candybar-gather-renderer-76bb.1dh.trm)

Medium review of #675:
- The confirmed case draws the ⚠ for a session no Claude Code ran in
  the same daemon, and the straggler case draws it once the old
  session's own run outlasts the race, so neither absence can come
  from a lane that is off or a dead lookup.
- The parts carry the journal turns the store is held by, the verb
  context logs into the tick's error check, and the argv is configFlag.
- The messages are asserted by pane, pid, record path and held session.

Kept as is: one rig per case (a shared rig couples the cases' clocks;
each runs well inside its timeout), and failing on warn lines (the only
ones are the stand-in pane's tmux refresh failing to spawn tmux). The
shared draw-parts helper is .5hr.

* test(lanes): the pane-draw ⚠ is asserted at error level, and any error the daemon logs fails its case (candybar-gather-renderer-76bb.1dh.trm)

Second high review of #675:
- The positive cases assert the session-pane entry's level is error, as
  the ticket's error list says; the negative ones assert no entry at any
  level.
- The logged-error check reads the whole log at every tick and once more
  after the last, so an error logged between ticks fails too; afterEach
  runs every cleanup before it rethrows.
- The verbs and the draw share one gates, launcher, sightings and held
  instant, as the daemon's do.
- The straggler timeline is fractions of the race, and the mismatch case
  is named for its run, not a rewrite it has none of.

Kept: the straggler's three ticks. One straggler cannot show the
rewrite-race exemption through the draw; breaking it still fails a case.

---------

## [1.209.0](https://github.com/promptctl/cc-candybar/compare/v1.208.12...v1.209.0) (2026-11-07)

### Features

* **band:** a switched-off band lane holds no follower process (candybar-animation-wbxz.w33) ([#645](https://github.com/promptctl/cc-candybar/issues/645)) ([c8e21dd](https://github.com/promptctl/cc-candybar/commit/c8e21dd0a0271567df669f0c7b81bc241551c07a))

fix(state): a session value its config no longer admits draws the default and warns (brandon-menus-sjhy.46w)

Session state outlives the config that wrote it. A stale value was swallowed
silently: the globals resolution dropped it, a placement's bar drew the saved
value while its carousel sat on its first option, and a carousel or cycle
folded an author key's stale value to its first member.

- The gate judges a stored value (Gate.verdict): a key one of the config's
  own `set` actions writes, holding a value its validator refuses or changes,
  is foreign. A key no `set` writes is the daemon's own and is held.
- JudgedState (src/daemon/foundations/judged-state.ts) is the branded reader
  every interpretive reader demands: the registry's `state` variables, step-
  state (which now steps from the seed instead of clamping), the verbs'
  settings picks, the closing view's closeNested, and the idle close's
  openRoots. Back admits a value only if the verdict holds it. Release reads
  after a reload stay raw.
- session.foreign (the session view) lists foreign values; the draw stands one
  amber `domain` warning per key, identified by its key.
- The ring shows a held non-option between the last and first options; the
  cycle keeps its rest-first reading, with the reason stated.
- validateBoolean accepts its own canonical false, "".
- placementSetting drops its fallback for a refused draft.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(facts): a shell or file source's key is a root of the declaration walk; one template enumeration; the undeclared read names what its site knows (candybar-gather-renderer-76bb.6pj.opl)

Review (high) findings taken:
- Every shell and file source is declared and its cache key evaluated whether
  or not a template reads it, so the walk seeds from those variables too; a key
  reading a built-in no placed segment read faulted the source before this.
- The unused-declaration check and the walk enumerate a segment's and a
  layout's templates through the same two functions.
- The undeclared read's message states what the reading site knows: the
  declaration its facts were gathered under does not name the fact, which is
  also true of a replay under a wider config.
- The rows' entries are built once, not per path.
- EVERY_BUILTIN had no production caller and lives in the test helper.
- Comments and docs: no socket arm exists yet; the declaration log line fires
  when a hold moves and the render event carries builtins= on every frame;
  §1 says each declared built-in; the memory paragraph said one thing twice.

Rejected, with reasons on the ticket: a whole-row read declares its parts
(an Undeclared inside a found object would be the silent hole the ticket
forbids); lead/trail are synthesis-only and never in the config the walk
reads.

feat(facts): a renderer declares the built-ins its config reads, and Gather gathers only those (candybar-gather-renderer-76bb.6pj.opl)

The facts document is complete over what the renderer declared, not total:
every declared built-in and source has a key, and nothing else does. The
declaration is one walk over every preset's placements, templates, partials
and globals rules, mapped through the payload's rows to the built-ins each
path reads; the doctor asks the same walk. The declared set is consulted once,
where the lanes are declared, and every later stage iterates the lanes it is
handed.

The payload is a table of rows, each composed from exactly the facts it names
(a compile error to read another), in one of two phases the type carries: a
turn row once per document, a draw row at the draw's instant (today). A read
of an undeclared built-in throws naming the variable and the fact, so the
segment draws ⚠ and check fails, never a blank. The render event and the
view-declared log line carry builtins=. FACTS_VERSION 2.

fix(config): undo puts a click's text back on the disk the click wrote; a write's stat error is never a cleanup's (candybar-testing-ihvy.5zt)

- The settings history takes the daemon's disk, and the config text read and
  write take a disk: a click, its proof, its write and its undo are one
  disk's. config-file-store leaves the systemFilesystem owners.
- writeAtomicOn takes the replaced file's mode before the tmp exists, so a
  stat that fails is the error the caller sees.
- config.md: ENOTDIR counts as absent beside ENOENT.

fix(config): a click writes its home on the disk it read and proved; the book's folder is absent as presence says (candybar-testing-ihvy.5zt)

- ConfigHome carries the click's writable disk; the commit writes through it
  (writeAtomicOn), so a click's read, proof and write are one disk's. Undo
  keeps its own system-disk pair until the settings history takes a disk.
- bookIsFiled asks presence(): a book folder that is a regular file holds no
  book, and the loose book is read.
- holdsGit asks presence() and marks its no-silent-failure exception; the
  ascent carrying the failure is candybar-testing-ihvy.izc.sv9.

fix(config): a click's proof shares the render cache's installed layers and reads its home's disk (candybar-testing-ihvy.5zt)

- ConfigHome carries the installed-layer memo its loads share; the render
  cache lends its own through the verb context, so a click's proof checks no
  plugin the bar's last load already checked. The memo keys on definition
  text, so a lent memo serves no layer the borrower's disk does not hold.
- presence() reads ENOTDIR as absent, as the stat it replaced did: a path
  through a regular file holds nothing. The filesystem contract pins ENOTDIR.
- A click reads its home's text and the layers above on the disk its proof
  loads; config-file-store leaves FS_READERS.
- The lane edge's fileExists asks the same disk as its presence.
- stateFromLoad folds into loadFromDisk; keyLoad is module-private.

feat(config): a renderer loads config as a value over the filesystem port (candybar-testing-ihvy.5zt)

Every read a config load makes goes through the FilesystemReads it is
handed: the answers book, discovery, worktree links, plugin folders, each
layer and each definition. readConfigLoad (src/config/load.ts) is the load
as a value; the render cache builds state from it. Each definition is read
once per load, and the installed-plugin memo is an owned value keyed on
the texts, not module state keyed on a stat. The answers book's read moves
into Config, the state-file store into src/disk. Repo-approval cases move
to test/unit over the fake. Ten files leave FS_READERS; Config gets an
import rule.
